mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) serves as a proxy for monetary policy stance; a high level (above 4.5%) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to elevated discount rates suppressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signals restrictive monetary policy that reduces corporate profitability and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate contractionary economic conditions that reduce consumer demand and business investment, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines > 0.5% YoY and HOUST declines > 0.3% MoM
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline as specified.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), a further decline in unemployment rate signals robust labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and consumer confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing economic output and corporate revenue, which correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of real GDP (GDPC1) above 23000 reflects sustained economic expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to elevated corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 is above 23000.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) indicates inflationary pressure in a 'hot' economy, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as central bank tightening accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), immediate market reactions to rate hikes cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced liquidity and risk asset rotation.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.
